corrections.why: The concrete tower was begun in 1906 and the Marine branch reports show it erected in 1908-09; sources give 1908 or 1909, not 1900.
The Quebec heritage register and the municipality use Phare de la Pointe-Mitis; Métis-sur-Mer Lighthouse is the village-based name.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1874 is the first wooden tower (lit 20 October 1874); the present concrete tower was begun in 1906 and entered service 1908-09.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on: completion of the concrete tower (1908 Lighthousefriends; 1909 local society, Quebec register; the Marine branch volume published 1909 already records it erected and the volume published 1910 records the new light); fog signal year (1917 vs 1918, May 1918 per local society); keepers 1906-1936 (Caron to 1936 vs Caron to 1931 then Laudry); Ouellet start (1965 vs 1970, which overlaps Ferguson 1959-70, so the 1965 start may be an assistant stint); light withdrawn 1997 vs 1999 (both on the local society's pages); first-tower cost 3,518.84 vs 3,518. Lighthousefriends' $3,000 for the tower conflicts with the $3,900 contract in the report. The Marine branch volumes are cited by volume year; fiscal years are given only where the text states them (1901, 1904, 1906). The 1906 keeper table (p.258) has columns printed as separate blocks: Jules G. Martin matched to Little Metis by adjacent position only. Parks Canada's DFHD statement pages did not load through the reader. The Quebec register states the sector was 'established in 1870' without explanation. The Amanda 1841 wreck is cited to the local society only (no independent source read). Keeper duties are cited as the society's general description, not as dated events. The 'Pointe des Monts' link for Fafard is per Lighthousefriends only. Not matched to the 'light' lens status beyond RPCQ and local society saying the municipality maintains the light.
